title: Session-lease coordinator & partial-token healing (post-incident remediation)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a regional capacity surge on 2026-02-27 we observed a class of streaming outages where clients received truncated or duplicated token fragments and sessions dropped without cleanly reconciling in the KV cache. The problem manifested as partial tokens (fragments) returned to clients and, in some cases, silent disconnects followed by immediate reconnects that caused duplicate fanout and KV cache contention. This ticket tracks the postmortem action plan: design and implement a session-lease coordinator, sequence-stamped token commit protocol, and improved telemetry to prevent recurrence.
root_cause_summary: A confluence of factors: (1) aggressive connection churn during a capacity pressure event caused our fanout layer to cancel and re-establish routes rapidly; (2) session expiry/cleanup ran on a tight timer and could remove close-to-complete token fragments before a client reconnect could reconcile them; (3) the token-assembly path lacked an idempotent commit boundary, so duplicate reconnects could lead to partial replays or duplicates; (4) backpressure propagation between serving runtime and fanout was lossy during peak GPU scheduling delays, allowing the serving runtime to drop partial outputs without triggering safe replay paths.
detection: On-call alerted via elevated error-rate and 'stream-output-fragment' alarm (PagerDuty PD-4321). Correlation with autoscaling logs and host-level OOM charts revealed sustained GPU queueing. Traces showed repeated session tear-down events within 15s windows and incomplete commit spans in the token-commit traces. Synthetic canary clients showed >5% session-continuity failures across affected hosts.
impact: ~1.8% of active streaming sessions during the 22:03-22:25 UTC window experienced partial-token or duplicate-token symptoms. Multiple production customers reported degraded UX (truncated responses, repeated phrases). No PII leakage. Estimated cost impact from retries and extra tokens ~2.4% additional token spend for the hour.
timeline: 2026-02-27 21:58 UTC -- autoscaling events begin; 2026-02-27 22:03 UTC -- first PD alert for stream-output-fragment rate; 22:07 UTC -- oncall isolates surge to region us-west-2 and increases session_lease timer as a short-term mitigation; 22:20 UTC -- traffic returned to normal; 2026-03-01 -- initial incident review; 2026-03-02 -- root-cause analysis completed and engineering action plan proposed.
short_term_mitigations: Applied a temporary session_lease extension from 15s -> 60s for affected fleets; enabled reconnect-handoff (server retains recent fragment tombstones for 120s); dialed down concurrent fanout retries to reduce duplicate commit attempts. These reduced customer-facing errors by ~70% in a controlled canary.
long_term_mitigation_summary: Design and ship a session-lease coordinator service that centralizes lease state for streaming sessions and exposes an idempotent sequence-stamped token commit API. Add explicit commit boundaries in the runtime so fragments are only GC'd after a successful commit ack. Improve backpressure propagation so serving runtime will stall token production when downstream fanout is overloaded rather than dropping partial fragments. Hardening will also include synthetic chaos tests that simulate rapid reconnects and capacity pressure.
action_items: A1: Implement 'conn-coord' (session-lease coordinator) that maintains authoritative leases and provides extend/release semantics (owner: Marcus).
A2: Add sequence-stamped token-commit API and make runtime token assembly idempotent (owner: Raya Singh).
A3: Add tombstone retention for partial fragments and a safe-GC flow gated by commit ack (owner: Marcus).
A4: Strengthen backpressure propagation: runtime -> fanout will return explicit 'stall' signals; no fragment drops during stall (owner: Systems Team lead: Omar Garcia).
A5: Create E2E synthetic test harness that fuzzes reconnects, duplicate fanout, and KV cache races (owner: SRE: Priya Nair).
A6: Add dashboard and SLO alerts: session-continuity-rate, fragment-gc-errors, commit-latency (owner: Observability: Leo Park).
A7: Run a staged rollout with canaries at 2 regions, ramp by host counts, monitor for regressions (owner: Marcus).
A8: Update client SDKs to perform sequence-aware reconnect handoff and dedupe fragments on reconnect (owner: SDK team: Elena Kovács).
design_decisions: We decided against making the KV cache single-writer per session because it would require global coordination and a large migration cost. Instead, conn-coord will be sharded by session-hash and provide cheap lease tokens to allow idempotent commits while keeping runtime horizontally scalable. We also chose sequence-stamped commits (32-bit sequence + session UUID) over full vector clocks to keep payloads small and reduce latency.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: unit/integration tests and feature flags (2 weeks). Phase 1: Deploy conn-coord in read-only mode for telemetry (1 week). Phase 2: Enable seq-commit API in canary cluster (us-east-1) for 48 hours and validate via synthetic load and customer canaries. Phase 3: Gradual region rollouts (us-west-2, eu-west-1) with 10/30/60/100% host ramps. Rollback plan: feature flag off and tombstone retention defaults revert to 60s.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: session_lease_renewals, session_lease_failures, fragment_commit_success_rate, fragment_gc_count, commit_latency_p50/p95. Alerts: fragment_commit_success_rate < 99.5% for 5m, session_lease_failures > 0.5% for 10m. Link to dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/streaming/session-continuity
tests_and_qa: Unit tests for seq-commit and idempotency, integration tests with simulated fanout duplicates, load tests at 3x normal traffic. Chaos tests to inject reconnect storms and delayed commit acks. Synthetic canary client that verifies no duplicates and end-to-end checksum on reconstructed token streams.
open_questions_and_tradeoffs: 1) How long should tombstones be retained by default (60s vs 300s)? Longer retention reduces chance of GC-induced truncation but increases memory usage. 2) Should we replicate conn-coord state synchronously across AZs? Synchronous replication increases safety but adds commit latency. We prefer async replication with a cross-check on reconnects for now.
notes: Customer communications team prepared a post-incident summary template and recommended outreach for high-usage customers. No regulatory concerns identified. We'll schedule a follow-up review after the canary ramp completes.
followups:
- Schedule cross-team demo of seq-commit semantics (owners: Marcus + Raya).
- Add SDK change to roadmap with estimate and client deprecation plan.
- Re-run cost modelling for token retry overhead after mitigation to update pricing impact estimates.
